newsitem.title: THAILAND: Asia should amend oil investment laws - BoozAllen.
newsitem.headline: Asia should amend oil investment laws - BoozAllen.

text.p: Clearer investment laws are needed in Asia to make it easier for multinational oil companies to invest in the region, a regional consultant said on Monday.

Robert Moeller, vice president of BoozAllen and Hamilton, an international management consulting firm, told Reuters foreign investment in Asia had been hampered by the fact that business laws were slightly different in each country.
Moeller said projected growth rates for all forms of energy and related products, such as petrochemicals, were larger in Asia than in nearly every other part of the world.
But several problems including the lack of skills in the region and clear legal frameworks remained an obstacle to energy growth.
"Regulatory structures, to control multiple players, are not yet developed," said Moeller after speaking on the first day of a two-day regional oil and gas conference here.

For example, he said Thailand requires multinational companies to enter into a joint venture with local partners in some businesses and they must also transfer technical skills to their local counterparts.

"The requirements are considered a good goal for the government to have but it's not always going to make the strategic alliance successful. It slows the success because local partners need to be more educated," said Moeller.
He said Caltex had been a long and successful strategic alliance in the energy sector. Caltex Petroleum Corp, which has many ventures in Asia, is a joint venture between Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
